subject: Inference interoperability — action items & parity tests
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
To: Sandeep Ramesh <sandeep@hyperapps.com>, Alex Morgan <alex@hyperapps.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Inference interoperability — action items & parity tests

Great conversation today — thanks again for the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can make the two parity tests you asked for (function/tool-calling and structured streaming) as actionable as possible. I attached a parity matrix and a lightweight Postman collection to accelerate smoke runs.

Post-call recap (high level)
- Your goal: replace current multi-cloud inference plumbing with a single runtime that preserves tool/function calling, schema-strict structured outputs, and streaming behavior while lowering token cost.
- Baseline endpoints to compare: HyperApps’ MegaCloud endpoint (your side), Redwood hosted inference (our default), and a reserved Dedicated node for performance validation.

Priority test suite (please confirm order):
1) Function/tool-calling smoke test (priority 1)
   - Verify call metadata (tool id, args) preserved in both sync and streaming modes.
   - Verify auth header passthrough and token exchange works with your internal tool runner.
2) Structured-output / JSON schema enforcement (priority 1)
   - Run with strict JSON schema; measure failure modes and partial-output recovery.
   - Test our "schema validation + repair" fallbacks vs Hyperscaler.
3) Streaming behavior (priority 2)
   - Compare chunk order, partial-JSON reassembly, latency per chunk (p50/p95), and finalization accuracy.
4) Latency/throughput parity (priority 2)
   - 1–8 concurrent streams with 512-token windows; target p95 per-token latency and end-to-end response time.

Deliverables we’ll provide this week
- Parity matrix (attached) with test definitions and measurement columns
- Postman collection and example payloads
- Proposed test schedule (see attached sheet)

Ask from your side
- Confirm who will own the MegaCloud endpoint and provide a short-lived test key (procurement can provide scoped creds).
- Confirm which output schema(s) you want enforced first (e.g., search response, order-ticket JSON).

Next suggested dates
- Lab run window: Tue 5/18 or Thu 5/20 morning PT — 60–90 minutes to run smoke tests and capture traces.

Thanks — I’ll coordinate resources on our side (Ben and Marissa will run the harness). If that timeline works, I’ll send a calendar invite and a short checklist for the MegaCloud credential handoff.

—Camila

From: Sandeep Ramesh <sandeep@hyperapps.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Morgan <alex@hyperapps.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 13:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Inference interoperability — action items & parity tests

Thanks Camila — this is exactly the level of detail we need. A few quick clarifications:

- Priority: we agree function/tool-calling and JSON/schema enforcement are top priority. Streaming fidelity is important but can be second pass.
- Credentials: procurement@hyperapps.com will provision a scoped key valid for 72 hours; Alex will share via the secure portal.
- Schema: start with the "order-ticket-v2" schema (we attached the schema in today’s meeting notes). If Redwood can do a strict-JSON pass + best-effort repair and surface a clear failure reason in the response metadata, that’ll cover our compliance needs.
- Success criteria (we’ll use these):
  * Function call integrity: 0 silent argument drop in 200 calls
  * JSON schema pass rate: >= 99% for strict mode on a 500-sample suite
  * Streaming chunk reassembly: final reconstructed JSON must be identical to non-streamed response in >= 99% of cases

We’re good for Thu 5/20 09:00 PT. Alex will upload credentials to the secure link and share the access ID here. Also copy procurement on the invite so they can timestamp the key handoff.

—Sandeep
Sandeep Ramesh | Head of Platform Engineering | HyperApps Inc.
sandeep@hyperapps.com

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>

Cc: Sandeep Ramesh <sandeep@hyperapps.com>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Inference interoperability — action items & parity tests (internal runbook)

Internal runbook notes (for the 5/20 lab):
- Test harness (we’ll use): local k6 runner + our streaming validator + the Postman collection Camila attached.
- Smoke test steps:
  1) Function-calling smoke (50 calls): verify tool metadata, headers, and callback URLs. Capture raw request/response and KV cache keys.
  2) JSON schema strict (100 requests): run with strict schema flag + repair-mode disabled to get failure modes.
  3) Streaming parity (100 streams): capture chunk timing, ordering, and parser-level errors. Run with both short (<64 tokens) and long (512 token) payloads.
- Observability hooks: enable token-level tracing and model variant tags (hosted vs dedicated). Export traces to /drive/recordings/5-20.
- Data handling: redact PII from traces; use synthetic order-ticket payloads.

I’ll own the streaming validator and results table. Marissa, please own schema enforcement tests and grab the "order-ticket-v2" schema from Sandeep when it’s available.

—Ben

Pre-reqs (please complete before start):

- HyperApps: drop the order-ticket-v2 schema in the Drive folder linked below.

I attached the parity matrix and a short post-call PDF with the timeline. Ben/Marissa will publish the raw results to the Drive folder within 48 hours of the run and follow up with a structured deck comparing MegaCloud vs Redwood (hosted and dedicated).

If procurement needs any paperwork or an MSA addendum to allow a short-lived test key, loop me in and I’ll expedite. Looking forward — we'll highlight where Evergreen fallbacks and streaming partial-repair give Redwood an operational advantage in the debrief.
